subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted `/exec` session defaults be allowed to loosen current global or agent exec policy after config changes, and what reset or migration behavior should existing sessions get?
rationale: Current docs and tests intentionally treat `/exec` as persisted session state, but the report shows that this can undermine operator expectations for global exec security changes.

options.title: Make config the safety floor
options.body: Keep `/exec` as a session convenience, but prevent persisted session values from loosening current global/agent policy and add cleanup coverage for existing stored fields.

options.title: Keep current session contract
options.body: Retain persisted `/exec` precedence and document that hard revocation must use tool policy, host approvals, or an explicit session reset path.

options.title: Expire exec overrides on config changes
options.body: Track a config signature and clear or ignore stored exec fields when relevant `tools.exec` settings change.

recommendation.title: Make config the safety floor
recommendation.body: Keep `/exec` as a session convenience, but prevent persisted session values from loosening current global/agent policy and add cleanup coverage for existing stored fields.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter introduced the `/exec` session override contract and later added the focused coverage that currently encodes the precedence behavior.
